chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Teaching Betty Riley and the Music Craft album with Miguelito
summary: Machito taught Betty Riley to sing Miguelito's numbers, then in California they backed Miguelito on a Music Craft album arranged by Rene.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yes. Well, that connection - Mr. Conn keep in mind the band because he never heard the band, but the band - Betty Riley, an Irish girl that was raised in Mexico, and she could sing Spanish, perfect. She came to La Conga, she followed Miguelito and she was there about two or three days listening to Miguelito Valdes. She said to me: "Machito, you could teach me or show me how to sing like Miguelito - "Babalu" and "Tierra Va Tembla"? I said: Well, if you have patience I think I could teach you. So every night when Miguelito finished the show, she used to go up there and we get into a different room and she played a good guitar and we start to gng, gng, gng, you know, until she learned how to sing those numbers the best she can and she was so grateful that she said: "One day I am going to pay you back what you did to me". I said, okay; so we went to California.
We spent three months up there. We don't do anything in Hollywood at all. No recording - oh yeah - we recorded with Miguelito at the Music Craft. We made an album with Miguelito.
So you are the orchestra that's backing him pu on Music Craft!!
But he can't use our name because we were signed with another company.
Yeah, but there was a guy that sounded like a pianist, like, you know .....
Renee, and he made the arrangement; so we made that recording and we came back to New York.
About what year was those recordings made?
Forty-fivé 'forty-six, while you were out there?
